messages:
incident-bot: PAGERCHECK: High error budget burn detected for us-west-prod at 2026-03-15T18:03:12Z — 5xx rate jumped to 18% over baseline, repeated 429->5xx cascade observed. Auto-pager triggered.
Maya Patel: saw it. dashboards show 429 spike right before the 5xx surge. rolling window points to the global rate-limiter.
Omar Khan: linking logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/us-west/5176549991 - getting a ton of "upstream timeout" and "client closed request" paired with 429s.
Liam Chen: my hypothesis — quota misweighting on the new rate policy v3 (deployed 17:58) caused token-bucket to drop requests, which cascaded into worker backpressure and timeouts.
Tess Alvarez: confirmed. config diff shows `rate_policy_v3` has per-route weight=100 (should be 10). That effectively reduced capacity for model-hosting routes.
Maya Patel: impact: multiple small-medium tenants experiencing elevated 5xx for text-generation and streaming. CS flagged 3 customers reporting timeouts. No DB issues.
Omar Khan: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) revert policy v3, 2) bump global token-bucket, 3) fail open route to small quantized variant. Which is fastest?
Liam Chen: fastest is bumping token-bucket via runtime toggle. Revert takes ~10m with CI checks. Fail-open to small variant requires routing change (5-7m).
Tess Alvarez: I can push a runtime toggle to increase `global_max_tokens` from 12k -> 60k. Command: 
```
rbctl runtime-set --key global_max_tokens --value 60000 --env prod
```
Maya Patel: go for it. make sure it's targeted to us-west first.
Tess Alvarez: running now against us-west pool only.
incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: Tess Alvarez executed runtime-set at 2026-03-15T18:05:09Z.
Omar Khan: monitoring... latency is dropping a bit, 5xx down from 18% -> 9% in 60s. 429s still present but lower.
Liam Chen: starting a targeted traffic drain to a warm spare region (us-east-2) for high QPS tenants to reduce pressure. That's a route-level change:
```
rbctl route-shift --from us-west --to us-east-2 --tenant-id tenant_442 --pct 30
```
Maya Patel: please include rollback IDs, set 30% then evaluate.
Liam Chen: done. Incident-bot: route-shift recorded.
Tess Alvarez: I also disabled the new leaky-bucket enforcement on /v1/generate for prod-us-west:
```
rbctl config-edit --path /policies/rate_policy_v3 --set enforcement=false --env prod --region us-west
```
Maya Patel: note: this reduces protection but necessary to stop cascade. We need to notify CS for customers that might see transient quota changes.
Omar Khan: CS notif drafted: "We observed transient elevated errors in us-west due to a rate-limiter config; we applied mitigations and expect normalized behavior within 15 minutes. We'll follow up with RCA." Sending to CS now.
incident-bot: Pager handoff reminder: current on-call is Lily (pager-oncall) until 2026-03-15T18:30Z.
Maya Patel: Lily is out of reach, paging backup (pager-oncall) — @pager-oncall you're owning the handoff in 10m.
pager-oncall: here, taking over. Good catch on the policy weight. Any persistent tenant failures?
Liam Chen: two tenants still have >5% 5xx, both are high-QPS. I've temporarily pinned them to quantized fallback `gpt-small-q4` which is less memory-hungry.
pager-oncall: acknowledged. I'll keep the runbook open. Can we capture a short impact matrix?
Maya Patel: Impact:
- tenant_442 (high QPS): intermittent 5xx, 40% of calls saw higher latency — mitigated by route shift.
- tenant_99 (mid QPS): 429s leading to client retries -> 5xx, currently at 6% error.
- public multi-tenant pool: increased latencies and occasional stream truncation.
Omar Khan: root cause short form: human error in rollout config where per-route weight was set 10x too high for other routes, starving model execution buckets and triggering backpressure -> worker queue timeouts -> 5xx.
Tess Alvarez: next steps: 1) create a hotfix to validate weight ratios pre-deploy, 2) add unit test for rate_policy_v3 thresholds, 3) schedule a revert audit.
Liam Chen: I'm opening a bridge: https://zoom.incidents/bridges/5176549991 (internal) — join for live debugging.
Maya Patel: CS: @Tess please include affected tenant list and ETA for follow-up notifications.
Tess Alvarez: on it. drafting message with TTL of 4 hours for follow-up RCA.
incident-bot: METRICS: 18:03 -> peak 5xx 18%; 18:06 -> 7%; 18:09 -> 3%. Trending to normal by 18:12.
pager-oncall: I'm taking lead for the remainder. Leaving checklist: confirmed mitigations active (runtime bump, disable enforcement, route shifts), bridge open, CS notified. Handoff at 18:10 to oncall rotation.
Maya Patel: thanks. Last action: I will schedule an incident postmortem and add preliminary notes in #postmortems. Add owners for hotfix (Liam/Tess) and RCA (Maya).
Liam Chen: quick artifact: log excerpt showing cascade pattern:
```
[18:02:58] proxy: 429 rate_limited route=/v1/generate tenant=tenant_99
[18:03:05] worker: queue_time=512ms -> exceed threshold, returning 504
[18:03:05] model-host: timeout waiting on kv-cache lock
[18:03:07] proxy: 5xx upstream_timeout route=/v1/generate tenant=tenant_442
```
Tess Alvarez: tagging the deployment that introduced the bad config: `deploy-2026-03-15/17:58:rate_policy_v3`
pager-oncall: leaving notes in incident timeline, moving to monitoring-only. If error rate climbs >5% again, we re-escalate to P1 and invoke full incident commander.
Maya Patel: closing the active mitigation loop. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
pager-oncall: :white_check_mark:
